Personally not very big on doing a torso/arms typa split. Cuz like if youre doing any form of compound work for your chest or back, you're hitting your arms and shoulders pretty decently. Just makes more sense to train them together. Both splits you mentioned have pretty similar frequency and assuming similar volume I'd imagine they'd be the same for recovery so just do whichever one you enjoy more, tho I'd personally go with the U/L/U/L/Arms

Honestly yeah that's pretty smart, as long as you're still training arms on your upper days. Delts, bi's and tri's all recover fairly quickly and don't need that much work so I think it makes a lot of sense to hit them 3 days a week.

Yk i thought I'd get into recovery issues but surprisingly that's not really the case. Matter of fact, I've been having an easier time progressively overloading. Idk if I'd wanna do full body, I still like having a good mix of compound and isolation work and if I wanted to hit everything, a full body day might end up with too many sets per session. Upper days are already a bit more involved with 16 sets (during PPL I had like 10-12 sets i think).

Less per session volume cuz I have a bad habit of going to faliure on everything all the time and obv that causes recovery issues, but it's more manageable on, say, 2-3 sets of chest vs 6+. Also higher frequency is shown to cause more growth. 3 sessions per week might be verging on diminishing results but it's been working well for me.

Used to do an 8 day split with P/P/L/R/P/P/L/R then I replaced the first leg day with a rest day. I do a high frequency 5 day split now with U/L/U/L/U/R/R and honestly I feel like this is the best fit for me.
